original.description: The overall goal of ARTES 4.0 Business Applications can be summarised as the development of pre-operational services - possibly in partnership - for a wide range of users through the combination of different systems. Business Applications activities aim at: i) collecting user feedback for better tuning of the applications and the operation of all elements involved, ii) developing commercial sustainable space based applications by linking user needs to corresponding solutions incorporating space assets requesting only limited technology adaptations, iii) demonstrating to users and stakeholders that the proposed solutions work in their operational environment and are compatible with their operational practices, iv) utilising at least one space asset (such as Satellite Communications, Earth Observation, Satellite Navigation, Human Spaceflight, or any other space asset, service or technology), leading to a better exploitation of existing space capacity and know-how together with a better understanding of how they should evolve to respond to user needs. ARTES 4.0 Business Applications operates via a 'Call for Proposals' which is always open. Partners respond with proposals as they find it opportune. The activities proposed in response to this 'Call for Proposals' must be relevant to above mentioned ARTES 4.0 Business Applications objectives. Although not a competitive tender action, this Call for Proposals' is published on esa-star Publication in order to achieve a higher degree of visibility. The closing date that is mentioned upon issue of the Call for Proposals is established solely for technical reasons connected with the esa-star Publication system and can be disregarded.

original.description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Science, Education and Youth of Croatia hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals (CfP), which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Croatian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types:Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use onfuture ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL 3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 150,000.Type B Product or Service Development activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all otheractivities).Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 5 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity.Type G1University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of nationalspace industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industryandwould lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 20,000.More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon itsissue date.

original.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims at accompanying the European economic operators in the Earth Observation market rapid evolution currently witnessed in Europe and overseas. InCubed offers a new process in ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the realization of endeavours near-to-the-market with Economic Operators. Activities to be supported include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (missions, instruments, prototype element of EO constellation), innovative mission management solution, including for future EO constellation, the development of application platforms, etc. InCubed is looking for commercial viability by the end of the activity (up to at least a minimum viable product level) and a substantial degree of innovation i.e. adding new value to the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement/involvement is mandatory. Commercial customers are encouraged to be either as part of the consortium representing the value chain or as beta testers/validators of the developed product/service.  Customer engagement/involvement must be highlighted at the pitch and proposal stage. Letters of potential customer support/interest are seen as a very positive aspect. The actual scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves in relevance to the InCubed objectives. Two development cycles are possible within InCubed: TheDe-Risking Cycle (start TRL 4) and Product Development Cycle (startTRL 6) depending on the maturity of the concept being developed. Regarding this forthcoming Announcement of Partnership Opportunity, Economic operators are invited to register and submit idea pitches onto ideas.esa.int (InCubed channel). Following a positive pitch meeting, the second step is to fill in a Part 1 (Outline) proposal template, which must be supported by the Participating State(s) having jurisdiction over them. Following a positive assessment,the economic operators will be invited to submit a Part 2 (Full) proposal template, as per established procedure and evaluation criteria. The proposals to be supported by InCubed will have to be co-funded by the economic operators (partnership agreements), as a sign of their engagement and belief in their own business case.

Activities to be supported include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (missions, instruments, prototype element of EO constellation), innovative mission management solution, including for future EO constellation, the development of application platforms, etc. InCubed is looking for commercial viability by the end of the activity (up to at least a minimum viable product level) and a substantial degree of innovation i.e. adding new value to the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement/involvement is mandatory. Commercial customers are encouraged to be either as part of the consortium representing the value chain or as beta testers/validators of the developed product/service.  Customer engagement/involvement must be highlighted at the pitch and proposal stage. Letters of potential customer support/interest are seen as a very positive aspect. The actual scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves in relevance to the InCubed objectives. Two development cycles are possible within InCubed: TheDe-Risking Cycle (start TRL 4) and Product Development Cycle (startTRL 6) depending on the maturity of the concept being developed. Regarding this forthcoming Announcement of Partnership Opportunity, Economic operators are invited to register and submit idea pitches onto ideas.esa.int (InCubed channel). Following a positive pitch meeting, the second step is to fill in a Part 1 (Outline) proposal template, which must be supported by the Participating State(s) having jurisdiction over them. Following a positive assessment,the economic operators will be invited to submit a Part 2 (Full) proposal template, as per established procedure and evaluation criteria. The proposals to be supported by InCubed will have to be co-funded by the economic operators (partnership agreements), as a sign of their engagement and belief in their own business case.

original.description: Under NAVISP Element 2, the Agency issues this permanently open Standard Call for Proposals without procurement, using Cooperative Agreements as contractual instrument.This Standard Call for Proposals without procurement aims to enhance Participant States' industrial competitiveness in the evolving Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) sector. Industry is invited to submit proposals to develop innovative and competitive PNT-related products. The Agency accepts proposals from both space and non-space companies, including large companies, mid-caps, small enterprises, and start-ups. Proposed products may address the satellite space segment, ground infrastructure, and user segment, including applications and services. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 2 team to discuss the development of pre-operational products aligned with their strategiesand plans. Details on the tendering process and how to prepare the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals without procurement documentation.

original.description: The European Space Agency and Xjenza Malta of the Republic of Malta hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals (CfP), which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to legal entities of Malta that are registered in ESA-STAR. This CfP foresees the following standard activity types:Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participationin ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 175,000.Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400 000 (hardware development)/EUR 250 000 (all other activities).Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 80,000.Type F Space (downstream) Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 250,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity.Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.

original.description: The ACCESS (Accelerating Commercialisation and Competitiveness of the European Space Sector) programme helps companies develop innovative commercial products and services that strengthen European competitiveness in both space and non-space markets. It fosters a diverse and dynamic space ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of commercialisation reach all Participating States.Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) is the element of ACCESS programme specifically designed to accelerate the transformation of innovative ideas into market-ready space-based services and applications that deliver measurable socio-economic impact.BASS offers to companies and academia derisking tools to mitigate technical and commercial risks, shortening the path from concept to market. With a strong user-driven focus, BASS creates the conditions for commercial success and positions space as a driver of innovation, competitiveness, and lasting value for society.To deliver these outcomes, BASS offers a comprehensive support package which includes zero-equity funding, tailored business and technical expertise, project management guidance, ESA branding, and access to commercialisation networks. This ecosystem connects companies with customers, investors, and partners, enabling them to overcome market barriers whilesecuring sustainable growth through private investment and demand-driven adoption.BASS support is tailored to every stage of developmentfrom assessing the viability of new space-based applications, to designing, implementing, and piloting space-based solutions and supporting their expansion into new markets.

description: The ACCESS (Accelerating Commercialisation and Competitiveness of the European Space Sector) programme helps companies develop innovative commercial products and services that strengthen European competitiveness in both space and non-space markets. It fosters a diverse and dynamic space ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of commercialisation reach all Participating States.Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) is the element of ACCESS programme specifically designed to accelerate the transformation of innovative ideas into market-ready space-based services and applications that deliver measurable socio-economic impact.BASS offers to companies and academia derisking tools to mitigate technical and commercial risks, shortening the path from concept to market. With a strong user-driven focus, BASS creates the conditions for commercial success and positions space as a driver of innovation, competitiveness, and lasting value for society.To deliver these outcomes, BASS offers a comprehensive support package which includes zero-equity funding, tailored business and technical expertise, project management guidance, ESA branding, and access to commercialisation networks. This ecosystem connects companies with customers, investors, and partners, enabling them to overcome market barriers whilesecuring sustainable growth through private investment and demand-driven adoption.BASS support is tailored to every stage of developmentfrom assessing the viability of new space-based applications, to designing, implementing, and piloting space-based solutions and supporting their expansion into new markets.
